brief: A 3D-printing station built from the starter base; the viewer is on the side of larger r. Frame, in one batch: raise the starter at q 0, r 0 to three storeys (place a two-storey base on it), and place full bases three storeys tall at q 2, 4, 6 and 8 on r 0, leaving the cells between them empty; in front, a one-storey row on r 1 from q 0 to 7, full bases at q 0 to 5 and half-n bases at q 6 and q 7, placed in the same batch so every column touches it. On storey 2 of each column add rod accessories (stem hex-acc-rod) on slot 0 and on slot 3 wherever an empty gap is beside it, then an axle (addAxle, slot 0) on storey 2 of the columns at q 0, 2, 4 and 6, and hang a filament spool on each axle with hang_spools. Top each column with a shallow divided bin (hex-bin-third-div3). On the front row: covers on q 0 to 3 as the work surface, shallow divided bins at q 4 (hex-bin-third-div3) and q 5 (hex-bin-third-div2), and drawers (key s) on q 6 and q 7, set open toward the viewer. Cap open faces and lock joints. Then fill every bin with heap-screws-div3 and heap-nuts-div3 using fill_compartments, leave the two open drawers empty for nozzles, and dress the covers left to right with a task lamp, a pencil cup, a hex driver set standing (hexdriver-set) and a hex key set (hexkey-set).

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
